info.label: More information
info.mode:
Learn: No clock. If you make a mistake, the app shows the right answer and asks that sum again later.
Play: The clock runs. Each mistake adds 3 seconds to your time. After a mistake the clock stops for 3 seconds so you can see the right answer. Try to beat your best time!
info.order:
In order: 1 × 2, 2 × 2, 3 × 2 … the way you say the table.
Shuffled: The same sums, but mixed up. Now you have to know each answer, not just the rhyme.
info.op:
Times ×: only times sums, e.g. 3 × 2 = 6.
Divide ÷: only division sums, e.g. 6 ÷ 2 = 3.
Mixed: times and division together. They belong together: if you know 3 × 2 = 6, you also know 6 ÷ 2 = 3.
info.which:
Tap the tables you want to practise. You can choose one table or as many as you like.
'All' picks all 12 tables and 'None' clears them again.
info.turnTables:
Off: the table number is always second, e.g. 3 × 2.
On: the app also asks 2 × 3 – the same answer, just the other way round.
info.turnMissing:
Off: the table number always stays visible, e.g. ? × 2 = 6 or 6 ÷ ? = 2.
On: the ? can also hide in other places, e.g. 3 × ? = 6 or ? ÷ 2 = 3.
info.count:
10, 20 or 30: that many questions, as fast as you can.
∞: Keep going as long as you answer correctly. The first mistake ends the round. How many can you get in a row? There are badges for 10, 25, 50, 100 and 150 in a row!
info.makeStep:
Add up / What's left: an ordinary sum like 6 + 3 = □ or 9 − 5 = □. Choose the answer from three numbers.
Number friends: part of the sum is missing, like 6 + □ = 9. Which number is 6's friend to make 9? Choose this when your child is ready for it.
Pick two: three cards are on the table. Tap the two cards that make the number together.
Pick three: four cards are on the table. Tap the three cards that make the number together.
With minus you take the smaller cards away from the biggest.
info.makeOp:
Plus +: add together, e.g. 6 + 3 = 9.
Minus −: take away, e.g. 9 − 5 = 4. How many are left?
Mixed: plus and minus sums together.
info.makeTargets:
Choose the numbers you want to practise.
In plus sums it is the answer (6 + 3 = 9). In minus sums the sum starts with this number (9 − 5 = 4).
In Pick two and Pick three it is the number you must make with the cards.
info.makePictures:
On: each number gets its own shapes – hearts, triangles, stars – in rows of 5. That way you can see and count.
After a mistake: the pictures only show when an answer was wrong, to help understand.
Off: numbers only.
info.make24How:
You get four numbers. Use each number once and make 24.
Tap a number, then +, −, × or ÷, then a second number. The two numbers become one new number. The sum appears under the card.
Keep going until only one number is left. Is it 24? Then you got it!
Whole numbers only: a division must come out exactly and you can't go below 0.
Undo takes back the last step. Start over begins again with the same card. Show me shows the easiest way, one step at a time. Skip brings a different card – the skipped card comes back later.
info.make24Level:
Every card has one, two or three dots in the corners.
One dot: the easiest cards.
Two dots: a bit harder.
Three dots: the hardest cards. Here it often helps to divide (÷) or to work with big numbers.
info.make24Big:
No: the numbers on the card are from 1 to 9.
Yes: the card can also have numbers up to 20, always with at least one number bigger than 9. That is harder.
The first time you choose Yes, it takes a moment to shuffle the cards.

help.title: How does it work?
help.parents:
For parents: sit with younger children the first few times they use the app. That way you both learn how it works.
Tap the i next to each choice for a short explanation.
